definitions.definition: (weaving) A tool used to carry the woof back and forth between the warp threads on a loom.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Job 7:6:
quote.text: My dayes are ſwifter then a weauers ſhuttle, and are ſpent without hope.

quote.citation: 1638, George Sandys, A Paraphrase upon Job:
quote.text: Like shuttles through the loom, so swiftly glideMy feather'd hours, and all my hopes deride!.

quote.citation: 2013 November 11, Claus-Dieter Brauns, “Food and Clothing”, in Mru: Hill People on the Border of Bangladesh‎[1], Basel: Birkhäuser, page 131:
quote.text: By placing the sword edgewise, the weaver keeps the countershed open, in order to shoot through the shuttle.

definitions.definition: The sliding thread holder in a sewing machine, which carries the lower thread through a loop of the upper thread, to make a lock stitch.
A transport service (such as a bus or train) that goes back and forth between two or more places.

quote.citation: 2012, Andrew Martin, Underground Overground: A passenger's history of the Tube, Profile Books, →ISBN, pages 76, 77:
quote.text: And until December 2010 the northern stretch of the 'Extension' featured a charming side-show: the Chesham Shuttle. [...] But the people of Chesham moaned about the shuttle: the waiting room at Chalfont & Latimer was too hot, or too cold; there were leaves on the line. [...] On 12 Dec 2010 the shuttle ceased operations and Metropolitan trains began to terminate at both Amersham and Chesham.

definitions.definition: Such a transport vehicle; a shuttle bus; a space shuttle.

quote.text: You're saying we take the parking shuttles, reinforce them with aluminum siding and then head to the gun store where our friend Andy plays some cowboy-movie, jump-on-the-wagon bullshit.

definitions.definition: Any other item that moves repeatedly back and forth between two positions, possibly transporting something else with it between those points (such as, in chemistry, a molecular shuttle).
A shutter, as for a channel for molten metal.
(intransitive, transitive) To go or send back and forth between two places.

quote.citation: 1982 April 24, Larry Goldsmith, “Freedom of Information: A Heterosexual Privilege?”, in Gay Community News, page 6:
quote.text: On several occasions during the next several months my attempts to see the logs were met alternately with this denial of their existence or a denial of my right to see them. After being shuttled from station to headquarters and headquarters to station, I finally consulted with GCNs attorney, John Ward.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To transport by shuttle or by means of a shuttle service.
